The Elder Scrolls Online (ESO) is the absolute gold standard for modern MMORPGs. It seamlessly blends the massive scale of an online multiplayer world with the deep, narrative-driven freedom of a classic single-player Elder Scrolls game. After hundreds of hours in Tamriel, I can confidently say this is the best MMO on the market.

[b]PROS:[/b]

*   [b]Massive & Varied PvP Modes:[/b] Whether you want large-scale faction warfare or tight team skirmishes, the PvP is incredible. You can join the Alliance War in Cyrodiil to siege massive castles with hundreds of players and siege engines, control the Imperial City in high-stakes PvPvE, or jump into fast-paced 4v4v4 Battlegrounds for quick combat fixes.
*   [b]Complete Play-Your-Way Freedom:[/b] Thanks to the "One Tamriel" system, the entire world scales to your level. You can travel to any zone (like Skyrim, Morrowind, or Elsweyr) right from level one and play with friends regardless of level gaps.
*   [b]Fully Voiced Storytelling:[/b] Every single line of dialogue in the game is fully voice-acted. Quests feel like genuine Elder Scrolls stories rather than tedious, text-heavy fetch chores.
*   [b]Dynamic Action Combat:[/b] No rigid, tab-target cooldown rotations here. Combat relies on active dodging, blocking, weapon swapping, and real-time skill execution, giving it a very high skill ceiling.
*   [b]Limitless Build Flexibility:[/b] Any class can use any weapon, wear any armor type, and fulfill any role (Tank, Healer, or DPS). You have total freedom to craft your ideal playstyle.
*   [b]No Gear Treadmill:[/b] ESO respects your time. Once you hit the Champion Point gear cap, your armor sets stay relevant. You can take a break from the game for months and return without your hard-earned gear being instantly obsolete.

[b]CONS:[/b]

*   [b]Inventory Management without ESO Plus:[/b] Managing your inventory can become tedious without the unlimited crafting bag provided by the optional ESO Plus subscription.

[b]FINAL VERDICT: 10/10[/b]
Whether you are a casual solo adventurer looking for incredible lore, a PvP veteran hunting for faction glory, or a hardcore player hunting for deep endgame progression, ESO is unparalleled. It is the most complete, polished, and rewarding MMO available today. Absolute masterpiece.

1400 hours on my non-Steam account. I have just finished Endwalker.

~Gameplay~
It really depends on if you like this style of MMO; it's a party-centric mission based system of going in and out of closed instance dungeons, fighting trash and 3 bosses. This is 70% of FF14's content, the rest being mini-games, roguelike dungeons, huge battle regions with alternative leveling, PVP and other stuff. 

For the main dungeoning think a perfected version of FF: Crystal Chronicles. A bit too formulaic/repetitive for my tastes. Starts off bland, but improves over the long slogging hours. The dungeons are the mainstay and slowly improve with every chapter/expansion.

Combat: You'll do most normal dungeons with 2 DPS, 1 Hear and 1 Tank. It centers around timing abilities between enemy attacks in sync with your allies to maximize damage while dodging AOEs and memorizing or interpreting enemy and boss mechanics. POSITIONING, TIMING and MEMORIZATION are key, especially in harder content. It's not for everyone.

Dungeons:
- ARR - Bland, weird, they've had to reformat a few of them. There are lots of odd, experimental mechanics. The main issue is the dissonance of length and mechanics, but that's also the charm sometimes.
- Heavensward - Improved with more streamlined mechanics, but still experimental.
- Stormblood - This is where dungeons started to become formulaic, but well made.
- Shadowbringers - This is where dungeons started to pick up in challenge AND storytelling in the midst of the dungeon
- Endwalker - Great, just continuing Shadow's trajectory
- Dawntrail - I've heard good things. 

Raids: There are two kinds; Normal and Alliance.
- Normal - A subsequent boss rush of 12 bosses with 8-players
- Alliance Raids - 3 big dungeons per chapter back to back in a 24-player group split into 3 parties.
Normal Raids are nice and quick. Many are well made, but sometimes you get a boss with confusing, mean or abstract mechanics in both Normal and Alliance (Cerberus's stomach mechanic, positioning around Eden Titan, Construct 7's math puzzle, etc.).
The worst part of Raids are not the Raid's fault, it's the queueing. You'll often queue up for old content, because new players are doing them the most. Fine early on, irritating later.

Bosses: You'll fight lone bosses later without dungeons before the fight. They come in 5 varieties (soon 6); Normal, Hard, Extreme, Savage, Ultimate. The latter 3 are optional. The latter 2 give great rewards, but are very difficult.
- Normal - What you'd expect, they're slightly harder than dungeon bosses.
- Hard - Really not much harder than Normal.
- Extreme - This is where content gets rough on new/unskilled players. They use similar mechanics as their Normal/Hard counterparts but can still take hours to beat.
- Savage - The chaff cutter. These bosses can take hours to days to do right. The mechanics are usually nothing like their easier counterparts. If you cannot perform Memorization and Positioning as mentioned earlier you cannot win, only scathe by with a few mistakes.
- Ultimate - The top. These can take days to weeks to perform and require deep understanding of loooong phases of fights with near perfect party synergy and no room for errors. People will get mad at newbs, it's part of the process.

Classes (Jobs): There are 3 groups: DPS, Healers and Tanks (Soon there with be Off-Tanks). This is where FF14 gets fun but also disappointing. FF14 has a huge problem with classes; they do not pop off and feel complete till Lv70, some not until 90! Basically no class will feel Finished until Shadowbringers. This is both a good and terrible thing; Good because you'll learn them over time and get a feel for every one over long periods of time like any skill.  Bad because that's far too long to have your whole tool kit and worse, some classes are only unlocked after getting to a certain level with another class so you'll get all its abilities dumped on you. I'll rate classes here I know well:
~DPS
- Monk - Simple. It's all about streaming combo chains into each other.
- Dragoon - Early on it's about maximizing damage on strong singular strikes that feel great to pull off.
- Ninja - Very high DPS if you're quick with controls. It uses a series of button combos that cause different damaging effects, but require accuracy and memory to perform.
- Reaper - Sleek class where you ramp up between 3 sets of combos into strong finishers. Has a satisfying rising crescendo feel.
- Bard - You have a series of strong ranged ability combos you juggle between party buffs.
- Dancer - Deals decent damage while buffing a single other player and doing mini-games to cause strong buffs.
- Black Mage - A difficult class that can deal a lot of damage. Its worst aspect is how much you must stand still while being targeted by AOES all the while juggling MP resource management. Hard, but satisfying to some. Easily earns the toughest class in the game title.
- Summoner - This class is NOT A PET CLASS. It is basically a simplified Black Mage without worrying about resources.

~Healer
- White Mage - Simple but effective, strong healing. Also surprising damage if you use its casting speed buff for damage.
- Scholar - Complicated in ways I cannot interpret nor specify.
- Astrologian - Great area healing, decent damage and very strong single target buffs. You'll do great if you can memorize and dish out the buffs to those who need them most.
- Sage - It's stand out for its being able to do a little bit of everything, even healing from doing damage. Beautiful cyber aesthetic.

~Tank
- Paladin -A very shield and mitigation centric class. Strange, but cool aesthetic reminiscent of Nomura's tattoo designs.
- Warrior - Simple. Self-sustain with damage reductions and decent damage. They are good at clutch wins after party wipes.
- Dark Knight - Weirdly low health, but with many mitigations and ways to stay up while dealing good damage. Beautiful dark, occult aesthetic.
- Gunbreaker - A very busy Tank class if you like doing more damage than the other tanks, almost like a DPS.

~Story~
I'll keep it brief for the sake of spoilers and this review's length and base it per chapter.
- ARR - Boring, but rises up to being interesting. Has good worldbuilding at least. If you can make it over this hill you're smooth sailing.
- Heavensward - Best PLOT (sound sequence of events), not Story (emotional context, though it's no slouch), in the game. Very good villains, second best hub town IMO, great character arcs, great ending.
- Stormblood - The first contentious chapter. It's not that bad, just feels like a Saturday Morning cartoon a little? There are 4 villains and 2.5 of them are cartoons, while the other is the best rival type villain in the game, she's also just one of the best written characters in FF14 in general. It flips between boring and exciting. The side characters are bland, but the new setting is a nice change of pace if you like Asian aesthetics.
- Shadowbringers - This is the chapter people play FF14 for. Two of the best villains in all FF, and one good one. Best hub town IMO. Best overall story arc with great, impactful moments and basically no character is wasted. Its main content ends incredibly then follow sup with Another great story arc before closing. My ONLY complaints are a small bit of slow pacing that's nowhere near as bad as ARR or Storm and it has the WORST side villain of the game.
- Endwalker - The chapter I was excited for most and severely dissatisfied with. It has the highest peaks of threat and conflict with the lowest valleys of story moments. It starts off agonizingly slow, then it's great up till halfway through before it crashes due to a writing trope that ruptures the story. I personally can no longer be excited about the game after this chapter, but cherish everything before that moment.

The worst part about the game's writing is the empty, slow, repetitive pacing and writing.
The best part is the peak moments after the slow crescendos

I'm leaving this review after having to purchase the stand-alone version of the game off of steam because my steam Sq Enix account became desynced at a time when my steam account was hacked - Sq Enix and steam were both unable to fix the issue so years after my steam purchase I decided to purchase again and give the game a fair trial.  My total play time is about 84 hours via my Sq Enix FFXIV launcher.

I love MMO's in general so my review should be taken with a grain of salt. 

As far as MMO's go, I dont think I've ever seen such a sprawling (massive) MMO, I mean this in terms of "land mass / areas to travel" and the number of people I saw online in any given hub. Maybe the area isnt "that large" but considering you have walk or travel by mount to every single teleportation aetheryte (beacon) it sure seemed huge. I would say at least 25% of the time I spent in the game was spent running or traveling, it went from :oh this is a cool zone" to "I'm so bored from just walking back and forth".

Compared to other MMO's this game is more of a story driven SIM than an action MMO. Leveling up, at least 50% of your in game time will be spent either trying to skip dialogue or trapped in non skippable dialogue.  If you love story rich, total immersion or role play type MMO's this game has got you covered.  If you like MMOs where you can just spend your day in rapid succession beating the heads of your enemies in, this game will not deliver.

Graphics are great , mobs are all unique, spells look awesome - I had zero complaints and for me a game lives or dies by its graphics - it could be the best game in the world if it looks like poop, I can't enjoy it. 

Thing's I did not like:  I did not like that the game was/is a LOTR simulation where you walk and talk walk and talk and eventually you get to fight something. I did not enjoy that professions in the game are not made for casual players, professions in this game are actually people who spend full days working their professions - even guides tell you that professions are not something normal/casual players can do because of the time investment required.  

I did not enjoy that caster classes such as my Black Mage , for the most part you have to stand still to cast all your spells. Eventually I got a few long cool down spells that for 5-8 seconds allowed me to cast while moving. I did not like that every spell shares global cool downs with other spells i.e.  cast a fire spell, the 2 seconds you have to wait before casting another fire spell is also 2 seconds you have to wait before casting the frost spells so there is no chaining of spells  - you are constantly wondering why global cool downs effect all spells no matter what school they come from - this is what actually drove me so mad that I stopped playing.

Overall, if you want a role playing game or if your a gamer that loves to be inside the story - this game is for you. If you want a game where you can just drop into dungeons, rinse and repeat (non stop action) and go back to a town for a break...this game is not for you - the majority of this game is the story happening in the world, not the monsters in the story, in the world.

This review is positive because there wasn't anything about the game that was bad, I am just not the type of MMO player that ever watches cut scenes or knows lore or cares about back stories.

The best MMO I've ever played. No FOMO - Horizontal progression means your gear stays relevant and you can play at your own pace. Set in a massive world with plenty to discover. It also plays surprisingly well with a controller using Steam Input. There are a lot of different currencies, which can feel overwhelming at first, though they're all gradually introduced through the main story and expansion arcs. I always find myself coming back to this game.

I wish I could give the game a "Yes, but..." rating. GW2 is an exceptionally fun MMO, and the fact that the core game is essentially free-to-play without predatory monetization is a miracle.

BUT, GW2 has two huge problems, and the first is an unexpected one: It's filled to the brim with stuff. That may sound like a weird problem to have, but it's a decade-old MMO, where Day 1 content lives alongside quite recent content. For everything you do, you get weird map-specific currency, with which you buy items, for which their use is not immediately apparent. The game has countless currencies and trinkets and items, and you constantly need to check the wiki to figure out what any of it does.

The second huge problem is "I just hit Lv. 80 and I have no idea what to do". To which the answer is usually "Whatever you want", which is not helpful. The game does a remarkably bad job at telling you what it is you can do, and you basically need someone to guide you through and show you the ropes. Without such a person, you will feel hopelessly lost, like you're always missing something.

You can’t sum up Guild Wars 2 in a few words, and that is precisely its greatest strength.

You are presented with a virtually endless amount of content, without ever feeling forced onto a set track. The best part is the absolute freedom of choice: you set your own pace and difficulty level, seamlessly shifting from relaxed exploration to challenging endgame content (Fractals, Raids, WvW), all without the classic gear treadmill that makes your progress obsolete with every patch.

What truly makes it feel like a real MMORPG, however, is the atmosphere:

- Total immersion: Standing alongside dozens of players coordinating to take down a colossal World Boss still delivers chills that few other games can match.

- A golden community: A friendly, welcoming environment with virtually zero toxicity. Veterans here genuinely go out of their way to help newcomers.

It’s impossible to explain everything it offers without writing a novel—the only way is to experience it yourself. Highly recommended, while eagerly awaiting whatever Guild Wars 3 will bring.

free-to-play (F2P) accounts cannot have permanent mounts. 
Here’s the exact situation  : Free-to-Play Accounts
When you reach level 10 (or the next multiple of 10 on older characters), you get a temporary 10-hour trial of the Raptor mount.
The timer only counts down while you are logged in and playing.
Once the 10 hours are up, the mount disappears and you cannot get it back without buying an expansion.
You cannot unlock any other mounts (Springer, Skimmer, Jackal, Griffon, etc.) on a pure F2P account.
How to Get Permanent Mounts : You need to buy at least one expansion. Any expansion permanently unlocks the basic Raptor when a character hits level 10 (or the next multiple of 10).

Without a doubt the best "tab targeting" MMO on the market and its not even close. The closest game to compare this to is WoW, the 'king' of MMOs, and I firmly believe this is a much better game in ALMOST all aspects. If this game had released the same time as WoW, this would be the king. The story line, world building, and overall lore in Tyria is just as deep as WoW if that is one of your main boxes to check. The class building, while I would not necessarily say is "deeper" than WoW, feels much more free as all classes and professions are viable in ALMOST every role whereas in WoW you pretty much always use the cookie cutter build that has been solved for 30 years. For example, you can make your ranger, warrior, or thief a healer with certain professions, something that is impossible in WoW. The combat IS much deeper in GW2, however. While WoW's main complexity and skill ceiling in combat relies almost entirely on rotation and knowledge alone due to there not being on demand block or dodge mechanics, GW2 has an almost action combat approach and even offers action camera. You have eye frames in the form of a dodge mechanic and specific abilities, on demand blocks in the form of aegis and certain abilities as well, many different combat buffs to upkeep that increase crit chance, power, movement speed, ability cd reduction, etc, a weapon swap system that, for some classes, offers 3 weapons to use and switch to, and all the other mechanics that WoW has. This makes the PvP scene particularly exciting as you don't have to ever abide by the rock, paper, scissors archetype that WoW offers. Regardless of class, on equal skill levels, you never feel as if a class just outright beats another like in WoW. You can also completely change up your class by simply switching what weapons you are using. In GW2 your main combat bars are determined by your weapons. One of the biggest examples is in the form of the ranger, a well known class in all MMOs that is almost exclusively a ranged class. Well, not in GW2. In fact, one of rangers best builds is a melee build in the form of one of its professions, Untamed. However, if you do really wanna lean into the ranger/bow role, Galeshot is the perfect profession for you. And the real kicker is you don't have to start a whole new character to play both. GW2 offers a very simple and easy system that allows you to switch to any of these professions at anytime, assuming you have collected enough hero points to unlock them. If the PvP scene isn't your preferred game-mode and you instead prefer PVE, GW2 also has you covered. Although, this is the one aspect that I would say WoW has a lead on if you're a hardcore dungeon/raid runner. Regardless, GW2 offers all your typical PVE content. Dungeons in GW2 are called fractals and increase in difficulty in the form of a tier system. I have not gotten into the raid scene so I won't speak much on it, however, it looks pretty fun and fulfilling. However, again, I would give WoW an edge in that sense. The OW PVE scene is undoubtedly better in GW2, though. Especially if you're the completionist type. You can spend 100's of hours alone simply completing the map and even more if you include regular events, meta events, jumping puzzles, etc. Achievement hunting in GW2 is also a huge part of the game and will always leave you with something to do which, again, tracks back to the game appealing to completionists. I have barely scratched the surface on all this game offers but I do think its enough to give whoever reads this some insight on what to expect. I cannot recommend it enough, especially in the depressing MMO scene that were left with today. It's also worth noting that the base GW2 game is completely free. Meaning you can always download it and give it a try without losing anything but time. If you decide you like it and wanna invest in the game, the Heart of Thorns/Path of Fire bundle is a great deal and offers many different professions, areas, and content to explore. You really have nothing to lose. If you find yourself wanting an MMO that offers a bit more mechanical complexity, interaction, and depth than WoW, GW2 is for you. Jump into Tyria and give it a go!

The game has a massive casual player trap midway through called The New War. Normally you play as a space ninja called a Warframe with high powered shields, or at least armor, super-strong weapons and special powers.

In The New War, you're suddenly stripped of all of that. Your high-powered Warframe, your equipment, given a minimum of no health, no shields or armor, and a very finnicky bow that they force you to use, which is trouble if you have no practice with bows.

You also don't get your good equipment back until two of three extremely difficult enemies called Archons are killed. If you get hit by their attacks, they will one-shot you. Even the common enemies will one-shot you in this part of the game.

It is quite literally Mission Impossible if you have a job that isn't "Play Warframe all day."

You're also stuck in the mission until you're finished. You're locked out of other content because it's apparently such a major story beat that they have to force you to play through this impossible mission instead of making it optional and giving it to you as a cutscene.

Oh, and if you get stuck, you *can* get out of it by asking the developers for support, but they will kick you out at a point *before* the mission and give you the ever unhelpful, "Git gud brah" as a reply.

And if you're going to try and say that there are strategies for that on YouTube, well, I tried those strategies. [b]They don't work.[/b]

When I first played this game in 2014 it was a genuinely unique experience with a unique blend of guns, magic, and melee options and interesting movement mechanics. The core gameplay elements were not overly complex, but offered a lot of ways to play and master. The story was vague and left a lot to the imagination, but it was at least fairly consistent and was not the focus. I'm not saying the game was perfect, but compared to what it has turned into it was magical, and for a while it stayed that way and improved. 

However, over time the game has become something else entirely due to every update adding content islands with confusing new mechanics, currencies, unclear objectives, and incredibly jarring power creep. The game has gone from a fairly fast paced shooter to a game where you don't aim at individual enemies and instead just cast an ability in the room you are moving through without even thinking. The movement overhaul they did, while fixing some of the issues it originally had, has made the game so fast to the point you are supposed to just bullet jump around instead of running.

On another note, there's the story and quests. Like I said, there wasn't much of a concrete story in the beginning, but with the direction they took it in each update, I honestly would have preferred that. Despite the fact that you play as a mysterious alien bioweapon and are slaughtering countless enemies in morally questionable ways, the tone of the story has shifted towards a weird attempt to address found family, childhood trauma, mental health, and other more nuanced themes, which in a different game and with better writing I'd have no issue, but the implementation is just incredibly jarring tonally, extremely melodramatic and forced. It just doesn't fit with the gameplay at all. 

Every time I have considered coming back, I am instead met with an increasingly mutilated shell of what was once one of my favorite games.

[h2]【ENGLISH VERSION】[/h2]
Battlefield is campaign-only for me. Story and music are decent, everything else is meh... Just watch a playthrough. Thumbs-down because bugs are game-breaking.
Bugs everywhere: collectibles you can't pick up or that vanish, subtitle/localization issues, random save wipes, crashes, CTDs. Invisible walls—you aim at an enemy, shots don't register, no hitmarker. "The Last Tiger" has mission/collectible bugs and no achievements. You only see level select and letters after fully clearing a chapter. Sometimes a level bugs out and shows challenges complete or letters missing before you start—or the menu shows zero progress.
Restart a mission without carrying progress and you lose your weapons (RIP my favorite loadout T.T).
The "letters" collectibles: [spoiler]I spent ages reading every one (translation made it rough), many hit hard—wartime humanity made me cry... I planned to write about each but the character limit said no. Challenges? Didn't bother—felt pointless. But some Easter eggs are wild. "Under No Flag": Britain formed the SBS (historically closer to early SAS)—recruiting total scumbags. Protagonist William Sidney Bridger is the son of a crook, Arthur Bridger. SBS officer George Mason sees something in him—Bridger screws everything up (prison was a botched bank job with his dad, who left him to take the fall) but never stops trying. Mason pulls him from prison into his SBS squad—a deal. Their dynamic is great: Mason treats him like a burden but shields him out of duty and a twisted mentor bond. Bridger's pride and self-redemption—proving he's not useless. "Hurry Up": Bridger boats to the drop point, then pukes. He rigs a makeshift bomb on a Stuka, it falls off without exploding, infantry has to down two planes, Mason gets wounded, they hijack an enemy truck and stuff the guy inside (hilarious). "Quick Raid": Mason's hurt, so Bridger solo's three objectives and scavenges meds—destroying an air supply depot and radar station. At the third letter spot, blowing a rock pile spawns an anti-tank grenade pistol (Easter egg). He calls for help on a German radio and exposes their position. "Onslaught": one challenge is "kill 5 enemies while Billy sings"—weird vibe. They fight armor/tanks/infantry/planes while Mason plays music and they sing—honestly sad, probably keeping each other from breaking (also why am I doing all the fighting while you slack off? D:). Mason yells "Hey! Don't shoot Bridger—only I get to shoot Bridger." Reinforcements keep coming, they think it's over, then the radio works—backup arrives! So hype. Mason makes another deal (probably keeping Bridger in SBS). Easter egg: the guy in the truck asks if anyone noticed him, lol.
"Nordlys": Norway under Wehrmacht occupation. A British commando raid gets wiped out, Astrid captured, some escape (Solveig Fia Bjørnstad, her mom Astrid, and German Lt. Weber all look great XD—if a character dies you see Solveig's dates: 1925–1943, she's only 18!). They sabotage German heavy water production. "Still and Silent": Solveig rescues Astrid, they scout the factory, destroy the substation and plant. Escaping, Germans corner them—Astrid hugs Solveig, says "I love you," and throws her off the bridge. I lost it. So she lives and can deliver the intel. "Caught in the Storm": Solveig solo's through a blizzard, the package blows away, she falls into icy water, climbs out barely moving, Astrid's voice wakes her, she sprints to a cabin, kills the Germans, collapses. "Wolf and Dog": she reads the package—not for her, but the resistance: "take care of my daughter." There's a paperclip inside; she puts it on (symbol of Norwegian royalist loyalty—wearing it was criminalized). She decides to destroy the German-held resistance files and heavy water herself. At the shipment, the cargo and Astrid are moved—she chases a truck on a motorcycle dodging rockets, a U-boat surfaces, Astrid blows it up with a grenade. Mother and daughter lock eyes. Astrid's thought: "I'm proud of you, Solveig..." I cried.
"Tirailleur": Allies liberate France. Told by elderly Deme Cisse—Senegalese soldiers who fought for France but never saw it, underequipped, unrecognized for decades. "Liberty": Deme and squad take ground. After the win, Idrissa Cisse (seems to be his brother) wants to hold (he has a wife and kid) but Deme wants to keep pushing. "Equality": Deme finds scattered squad members, sees captured soldiers executed, wonders if he's too late. Idrissa says the squad's too depleted; Deme wants pressure. "Fraternity or Death": Deme pops a flare, clears the village, takes the manor—Deme says they shouldn't go in. Idrissa drags him from a tank; Deme watches Idrissa jump onto the tank with a grenade and die—we see it from Idrissa's POV. They take a photo (why do all soldiers have the same face? XD), but later Deme says after liberation, Black soldiers were cropped out.
"The Last Tiger":[/spoiler] didn't finish because of bugs—too mad. Will update later, but I don't want to touch this game now.
I looked up the real history. War destroys everything and creates heroes—some recorded, some forgotten. Respect to everyone who defended their homes. May there be no war, may there be peace. Why do humans kill each other? Using what we built to destroy ourselves—would the world be more beautiful without us?

战地我只玩单人战役。剧情音乐还行，其他真不行……只推荐云通关。差评原因：Bug多到严重影响体验。
单人战役恶性Bug太多：收集品拾取不了或消失；字幕汉化问题；动不动丢存档、崩溃、闪退；有空气墙，瞄准了打不中没提示。“最后的猛虎”有任务/收集品Bug且没成就；章节全通才看得到关卡选项和信件；有时进关卡显示挑战已完成或没信件，实际却没有，界面进度也是空的。
不继承进度重开任务，武器就没了（我就这样丢了顺手武器T.T）。
“信件”收集品：[spoiler]我花了好久一字一句看（翻译影响观感），很多信让人难受（战争人情世故，想哭……）……本想逐封写感想但字数上限。挑战没特意做，感觉没意义，但有些彩蛋耐人寻味。“单枪匹马”：英国组建SBS（原型早期SAS），招的全是坏蛋。主角William Sidney Bridger是大坏人Arthur Bridger的儿子，SBS军官George Mason看中他总搞砸事（进监狱是因和爸抢银行被丢下顶罪）也不懈努力，把他捞进小队——一场交易。两人互动有趣：梅森嫌他累赘，又出于责任和扭曲师徒情护着他。布里杰的自尊与救赎，证明自己不是废物。“冲锋陷阵”：布里杰坐船到地点就晕船吐了。在斯图卡上装炸药，结果从机翼掉了没炸，两人对战，步兵打下两架飞机，梅森负伤，两人劫了敌人车把人塞进去（太逗）。“快闪屠杀”：梅森负伤，布里杰单人处理三个地点并找药：摧毁敌军空军补给站/雷达站。第3个信件位置炸石堆出反坦克榴弹手枪（彩蛋）。最后用无线电求援，位置暴露。“猛攻”：有个挑战是“比利唱歌时击杀5名敌人”。位置暴露后打装甲车/坦克/步兵/飞机，梅森放歌两人唱歌——挺悲伤，战斗时不让自己垮掉吧？（我一人打架你偷懒？D:）梅森在主角中枪时说：“不准冲布里杰开枪，只有我能冲布里杰开枪。”以为要完，无线电真叫来了自己人！很激动！之后梅森又做了个小交易。彩蛋：被劫车里的人问有没有人注意到他哈哈哈。
“北极光”：挪威被占，英国突击队+反抗军突袭覆没，阿斯特利德被俘（Solveig Fia Bjørnstad、她妈Astrid、德国韦伯中尉都好看XD；角色死了能看到苏薇1925–1943，才18岁！）。破坏德军重水设施。“静止不动”：苏薇救下阿斯特利德，调查工厂，摧毁变电站阻止重水生产。逃跑被堵，阿斯特利德抱住苏薇说“我爱你”，把她丢下桥——我没绷住，好难受。为了让苏薇活下去送情报。“往事如烟”：苏薇独自送包裹，暴风雪吹跑包裹，她坠崖掉进冰水，爬出后艰难前行，倒下时阿斯特利德的声音叫醒她，拼命跑到屋子杀敌又倒下。“狼与犬”：包裹写着“照顾好我女儿”，里面有个曲别针，她戴上了（象征挪威王室爱国意志，当时属犯罪）。决定自己摧毁情报和重水。发现货物和阿斯特利德被运走，骑摩托追卡车躲火箭弹，潜艇来运重水，阿斯特利德用手雷炸毁潜艇，母女对视，她心里说：“我为你骄傲，苏薇……”泪炸了。
“步兵团”：同盟国解放法国，老年Deme Cisse叙事，为法国而战却未见过法国的塞内加尔士兵，牺牲得不到承认。“自由”：德莫和队友夺取占领，胜利后Idrissa Cisse（似乎亲哥）决定驻扎（有老婆孩子），德莫想继续战斗。“平等”：德莫寻找队友，目睹被俘队友被处决，占领后伊祖沙认为不该无支援推进，德莫认为该出其不意。“博爱或死亡”：德莫发信号弹指挥，清理村庄占领庄园，德莫说不该进，伊祖沙把他从坦克旁拖走，德莫亲眼看到哥哥拿手雷扔进坦克同归于尽。后来合照了（为啥黑白人士兵脸都一样？XD），但德莫说解放后照片里黑人被撤掉了。

Best of Battlefield. No ands, ifs and buts. Period. Not to belittle Battlefield 4, let me explain: The movement, the maps, the flow of the maps and rotations, gunplay, individual character of the guns, the balance among the four classes and how well they match the guns and gadgets, the tanks, the planes, the sounds and the outstanding visuals. You might argue the same for EARLIER (pun intended) titles such as BF4. But BFV is a more modern game than BF4, with visuals far ahead of its time and without requiring a very expensive PC to play. Also, the music is brilliantly composed and beautifully recorded by real musicians. To be fair, you might call this a matter of taste. And I just prefer BFV. I like the humour in BFV and how it is sprinkled into the crazy real "Battlefield" situations which can happen around you with planes crashing just in front of you and flying parts of exploding tanks and what not. The sounds also include soldiers speaking in their native language, adding to the soundscape in which you navigate, and letting out funny little screams when they are killed. If you understand German, you are in for a treat - But I don't know about Japanese ;)  Also, the footsteps are directional and useful, unlike a title like BF6, which still lacks proper hit registration and has yet to demonstrate a server browser, which BFV does have. BFV is still played by a faithful and friendly player base - It's tough if you "only" have 2000 hours like me and no previous FPS experience, but a fun challenge. There is also the Combined Arms, in which you play against bots, so you can exploit it as an advanced shooting range to sharpen your skills and get comfortable with weapons and movement and get to know sections of five maps to give you a head start on Multiplayer. The game also includes EA Javelin anti cheat. Some players report difficulties with this, but it is still maintained in BFV. I only had a few passing problems. Sure BFV has a few bugs. But when you learn the workarounds its doable. And is there any flawless game after all. Finally, the skins are mostly respectful of an immersive WWII experience, or frankly any military setting, unlike certain other games. Oops, did I just review another game too? I am still earning the skins in BFV and they feel worthwhile getting. In conclusion, you might argue that BFV is the last great Battlefield game. It is a hidden gem because it was very misunderstood in its time. I hope that they will keep the servers alive just a little longer... Best regards :)

I do not recommend buying EA games. Everything EA makes is garbage.
I purchased this game three years ago and never played it for a single minute. When I launched it for the first time today, I found that EA added the Javelin kernel-level anti-cheat in a later update, which enforces Secure Boot. Older machines are locked out and cannot launch the game. Many motherboards for 9th-generation Intel CPUs and earlier do not natively support Secure Boot. I spent a lot of time going through every option in the BIOS, but there is no solution at all.

Even if you have a new computer that meets the Secure Boot and TPM 2.0 requirements, do not think everything will be fine. This kernel-level anti-cheat has many problems: it easily causes blue screens and crashes, conflicts with various monitoring programs and peripheral drivers, carries a high risk of false positives, and imposes extremely strict background restrictions.

This mandatory requirement did not exist when I purchased the game. The developer unilaterally added this gameplay restriction afterward. You pay for the game, but whether you can play it is entirely up to the anti-cheat. Both new and old computers can run into problems.

This one-size-fits-all approach shows no respect for players’ genuine financial support. I will not buy any games produced by EA in the future.

Battlefield 1 has a lot to unpack, so I'll try to keep it compact.

The Theme/Vibe:
My God... is it good. If anyone out there ever wanted Battlefield to be "serious" then this is the game for you. I'm not sure what team on Dice or EA back in the day decided that out of everything, WW1 would be the topic they took "seriously" but we NEED that team back. This game truly tries to carry over the dread and horror of WW1 in a Battlefield style and it honestly perfected it. You can feel it in the Campaign AND the Multiplayer.

The Campaign:
Battlefield isn't a franchise best known for its Campaigns, but BF1's war stories Campaign is easily a standout from the rest. The Campaign is worth every second spent playing it.

The Multiplayer:
I'm a guy all for nostalgia and I'd love to debate which Battlefield game has the best multiplayer, but if we removed nostalgia from the mix... I think BF1 might be the peak of the franchise. Some things have been omitted from previous installments which would have been nice to keep, but the trade-off was worth it imo. Operations might be the best gamemode the franchise has ever seen. The only major downside is the age of the game's toll on the playerbase... as with many older games, the dedicated players are numerous and very skilled so new players be warned.

The Performance/Graphics:
It's a 2016 game made for consoles. If you struggle to run this game, that's on you. The performance, along with the port to pc, is great. The graphics are honestly beautiful for its age, it easily keeps up with today's games.

Rating:
Compared to previous installments?: 8/10
Standalone?: 9.5/10

This game feels like they felt the need to reinvent the wheel instead of improving what they had. Payday 2 should have been the basis for payday 3 but instead its a very different game that seems to have the same issues as its previous installment in the series but also has a plethora of new issues. Like its previous installment we have a stealth issue, we have a lack of variety of ways to do it, in 2 we had two ways, the true slow methodical method and ecm rushing, in 3 you have a single build and it feels rather restrictive. The game suffers from the continuous issue of attempting to balance stealth and loud gameplay instead of integrating them, the skill system is the real issue, the way its formatted is the issue, we have a singular skill tree set of points when we really should have had three separate sets of points to cover the three aspects of the game, combat, stealth and assets. The lack of perk decks means sadly everyone plays the exactly the same and you see very little variation. Speaking of variation there is an extreme lack of that in the weapons, there is one singular smg side weapon, in 2 we had dozens, further issues arise when you look at the details of the guns and its actual gameplay, with the lack of detection we have a bunch of stats that the weapon mods do nothing for the most part, while we had actual visible differences and actual changes to gameplay in 2, and it was simpler to understand as you got actual numbers to look at and each had good and bad attributes and it was rare for them to only have good attributes. There is also a clear lack of masks and outfits compared to 2. Additionally we have no melee weapons, we have a lack luster melee push that does jack shit, we can take people as human shields but that doesnt really do any good, you cant convert or give stockholm syndrome, being able to shoot all locks as a barebones everyone can do really makes lockpicking not very useful, the saw being a special weapon instead of a tool and sometimes weapon also means we wont be getting the ever useful watch. The game feels barebones still after 3years, there is a lack of live action segments, there is still a lack of explaining the events from the end of the last game, or where exactly in the story the texas and mexico stuff happened since they happen before the white house but no real clear spot in the timeline from what i can see and they feel like pretty important parts to the story. We also have the elephant in the room of difficulty curve, with only 4 difficulties in this compared to the 7 in 2(technically 8 if we count one-down), the game suffers from the same issues of certain situations are unwinnable, about as annoying as the sniper spam in 2. It needs to be touched on the issue of the controller scheme, as is the game is unplayable on 360 controllers due to how the dpad works there, you end up throwing grenades when telling people to get down and you constantly forget x is throw equipment, we need to be able to remap the controls so that its closer to 2 in button layout because as is muscle memory takes over and mistakes constantly happen at the worst times. Payday 3 is essentially a sequel in name alone, taking place a decade after the white house heist, they never touch on the zombie issues or the other things in the connected universe that Payday2 made, we have a barebones roster of heisters, no real answers as to where anyone went off to, no safe house, no bobblehead bob bartending, no john cleese butler, no explaining how tony faked his death in the 80s, or really so many things unexplained that should have been gone into. Don't get me wrong the game isn't bad per say it's just not the experience I think anyone really wanted from a sequel to one of the greatest team games of all time. Now for a few positives, I do like how you buy attachments, colors, and pretty much everything once, I like several of the returning special cops, taser is as annoying but also has a case of being useful since you can shoot his battery pack, the dozer actually feels scary now, meanwhile the sniper and cloaker feel identical though the cloaker feels squishier. The game is really only as good as the company you play with, most people in the lobbies prove that sadly. I can only suggest this game to people if it is at least 70% off, and if you are a diehard Payday 2 player id say steer clear until they fix this game more because as is its still too foreign from 2.

I really wanted to love PAYDAY 3, but I just can't recommend it.

I've always loved the PAYDAY franchise and its whole concept. I spent so many hours playing PAYDAY 2, so naturally, I was excited for PAYDAY 3. I genuinely wanted to enjoy this game and recommend it to others, but unfortunately, I just can't.

My biggest issue? The lack of host migration and how easily your time can be wasted by other players.

If you're someone like me who doesn't have friends interested in playing PAYDAY 3, and you're planning to play through Quick Match with random players, I'd honestly recommend staying away from this game.

Let me explain why.

Imagine joining a heist, spending 30 minutes or more working with your teammates, carrying bags, helping with objectives, fighting off enemies, and doing everything you can to make sure the mission succeeds.

You're finally at the extraction point. The heist is practically over, and you're about to collect your rewards.

And then... you get kicked.

Just like that. All that time you spent helping your team? Gone. All your effort? Wasted. You get absolutely nothing.

And the worst part is that, in my experience, this isn't some rare incident that happens once in a while. I've encountered this behavior repeatedly, to the point where I genuinely started expecting it whenever I joined a random lobby.

I don't know what it is about this community, but some players seem to find it hilarious to kick someone right before the mission ends. You could be the most helpful teammate in the world, and it wouldn't matter.

Now, here's where my biggest frustration with the developers comes in.

Why on earth is there no host migration or some kind of protection against this?

For anyone unfamiliar with host migration, it's a feature that allows a multiplayer session to continue under a different host when the original host disconnects. Games like Helldivers 2 have systems that allow players to continue their missions when the host leaves.

I understand that host migration alone wouldn't necessarily solve every problem with being kicked, but a system that lets you continue your heist, or at least protects your progress and rewards, would make a massive difference.

Instead, you're completely at the mercy of other players. Someone can decide they don't want you in their lobby anymore, and suddenly, everything you've worked for is gone.

And that's what frustrates me the most. The game gives players the ability to waste someone else's time without offering the affected player any meaningful protection.

This is a cooperative game. The whole point is to work together, complete heists, and have fun with other players. But how am I supposed to enjoy playing with random people when I'm constantly worried that someone will kick me at the last second?

I genuinely don't understand why something as important as host migration, or at least a proper system to protect players from losing their rewards, isn't a priority.

We're talking about a modern cooperative multiplayer game. These kinds of quality-of-life features shouldn't be an afterthought.

And before anyone says, "Just host your own games" or "Play with friends," that completely misses the point. Not everyone has friends who play PAYDAY 3, and Quick Match exists for a reason. I shouldn't have to avoid playing with random people just to make sure my time isn't wasted.

What makes this even more disappointing is that I actually love the gameplay and the concept behind PAYDAY. I wanted this game to succeed, and I wanted to enjoy it as much as I enjoyed PAYDAY 2.

But after repeatedly having my time wasted, I eventually uninstalled the game, and I haven't touched it since.

It's a shame because I really wanted to love PAYDAY 3.

Until the developers introduce some kind of protection against this behavior, whether that's host migration, reward protection, or a better kicking system, I simply cannot recommend this game to anyone planning to play primarily through Quick Match.

A cooperative game shouldn't make you regret cooperating with other players.

When PAYDAY 3 released 3 years ago, saying that I was disappointed was an understatement. I felt so sad that I could not engage in any type of Payday content for years I was so ashamed. Seeing the community in shambles and furious with the numerous changes was hard to watch, both as a player and someone who tried to understand the devs point of view (mostly relating to the whole online only situation tied to the company's decisions about the game). But in retrospective the outrage was justified and necessary. 

Through time I took a peep from the sidelines to see how things where doing but never in detail, always fearing it was all over for my favourite franchise. But through thick and thin both the new and old dev team never gave up and stuck with the game, even giving the prequel to be devved and maintained by modders which is awesome and unexpected in modern gaming. 
I decided to give it a shot during the recent free weekend and it just felt right this time. For sure there are still some elements that i would change or dont praticularly like but the most important part is that I'm actually having fun with the game. I can finally play by myself, offline, with full pause capabilities and have fun with the game.

I like that some heists can be completed in casing mode, giving more challenge, even the new skills have more QoL or mechanics that make stealth more fun for someone like me who wasnt really that into it in the prequel. Absence of Concealment also is fun, maybe at lower difficulties the most, but starting a heist in stealth and then going loud can also be fun. 

Removing the need for a Nebula account was also a great move, along with making heists free for all with the new campaing mode. 

There is still the issue of having a lot of dlcs but I guess it was to be expected. Regarding crimebonds it is still a new concept, tho i would like to be able to purchase the whole thing by grinding optionally instead of having to spend real money for it, but if this is the way to keep forever out an ingame "premium cosmetic shop" then so be it.

So yeah, I'm glad we're here and cant wait to see what the future holds. I need my payday [strike] too [/strike]

I want to love this game. In many ways, I do love this game. But buyer beware, it has some serious drawbacks.

I know the game suffered from quite a few problems at launch. I'm not that familiar with those problems, and I will not be addressing them here. I will only speak to the game in its present state.

PROS: 
- Stealth feels a lot smoother. In 2, stealth could often feel a bit jagged, and there wasn't a whole lot of ways to approach it. While the optimal builds for stealth are still very "meta", the stealth mechanics feel a lot more involved now, and less like an afterthought.
- The missions feel more focused than in 2. In 2, any mission (apart from forced stealth sections) could become an absolute slaughterfest that would make most zombie shooters blush. The mechanics for loud play feels a lot more like actual *robbery*, which I personally enjoy. But don't worry, it's still ridiculous.
- Apropos the two points above, the transition from stealth to loud feels a lot better, as well. In 2, failing the stealth usually meant your entire build became useless. But if you're deep in a heist, blowing the stealth isn't necessarily an instant restart. Yeah, combat is harder, but still doable if you only need to hang in there for the final stretch. This makes gameplay feel more spontaneous and less frustrating.
- The way the environment reacts to the players feels more dynamic and less scripted, which helps all of the above points.

CONS:
- The DLC and pricing scheme is stupid, but we knew that already. Just be aware, THE BUNDLE DOESN'T INCLUDE THE LATEST DLC CRIMEBONDS. I got burnt on this.
- The information the UI gives you is about as consistent as Bain's meth cooking guidance. While certain traits and skills are well-explained and easily understood, how things like armour, armour penetration, and armour plates work is barely mentioned, let alone explained properly. Given that entire skill trees are built around these things, I cannot shake the feeling that the devs barely understand it themselves. This also makes the meta incredibly frustrating if you like experimenting with builds, as many crucial stats are *never shown* and also incredibly tedious to figure out - and even then, any data you get is incomplete. And by the size of this paragraph, you can probably guess it's my pet peeve. So, moving on!
- The wiki for this game is horribly outdated, making the above problem that much worse. Not that I blame the community; given how opaque some aspects of the game are, it feels like it would be a sisyphean task.
- Despite some of the rougher edges having been smoothed out, the game is still about as buggy as Puumba's breakfast.

So there you go. I am giving the game a thumbs up because I enjoy it, and the updated aesthetics are good. But it remains a mixed bag. If you want to try it, I recommend waiting for a sale.

PAYDAY 3 is an interesting game, because they did new things here that I feel could have been fun mechanics if combined with PAYDAY 2's endless bath of content. However, PAYDAY 2 some time in the past few months added incredibly invasive anti-piracy for a game I already paid for, despite being okay with DLC unlockers for years with catches that didn't affect players until now.

So instead of playing PAYDAY 2's wonderful gameplay, I bought this and tried it for the free weekend. And while this was still really fun of a PAYDAY game, I would have given this a mixed review if I could have. But since Steam only allows you to say "recommend it" or "don't recommend it", I have to give this a dislike for a couple of gameplay reasons.

PAYDAY 3 tries many cool mechanics that you don't see in PAYDAY 2, such as two equipment slots, an overkill weapon choice, subtle changes to gameplay flow (a "final charge" endless phase, different and flawed difficulty scaling, new negotiation phase) and overall changes to gunplay and feel. And while I feel a lot of these changes were a big highlight of the experience, there was not enough content to justify them being fun long-term. There's a few heists, most of them being Campaign content, and once you're through you just have to kind of replay them until the end of time. With PAYDAY 2, there was so much DLC content and heists that you had years of free content to catch up on. Here, once you beat the campaign, you're kind of finished overnight.

They also ruined a lot of what made the original guns awesome: the attachment system. I'm not going to lie, the old attachments menu was pretty nasty and I do appreciate the new way it works here. However the attachment selection is inferior, especially in the attachments department. I feel I'm being punished for taking more ammo with no way to have the best of both worlds. We really didn't need a minature Call of Duty built into PAYDAY. The old system was fine. If it was too powerful, add more debuffs, don't standardize the attachment system.

There are also many other degrations such as the modding experience, no "offline" experience, etc. And while these are big notes, they are somewhat excusable since they're a part of the "new" game instead of being sledgehammered in the old game. However this also kind of dismisses what made the original games great. Though they also do some good things in between, such as implementing some features from existing PAYDAY 2 mods (showing buffs). 

I had a fun time with this game, however the surprise and RNG that made PAYDAY 2 really good is no longer here. And with PD2 now being invasively overprotective, I cannot recommend this to hardcore PD2 players at all. Some beginners to the franchise can expect to have some fun, however if you can somehow get your hands on a copy of PD2 with all of it's DLC, including DLC that is no longer available, that will be a far better experience for you content-wise.

As an open world modern techy-hacking-shooter game, its a good 7/10 
As a Watch Dogs sequel to the original game, its a mediocre 5/10 that becomes buyable if its on sale 

Here are the main issues of the game coming from someone who really enjoyed the 1st watch dogs game and therefore is comparing this one through the lens of the first one 

1)  The characters are NOT interesting... In the First Watch Dogs you had the trio of Aiden Pierce as the enforcer, Clara as the hacker, and T-Bone as the old school combo of the two. Their collective dynamic is interesting, and when one of them dies in the first game, an impact is felt. The main villains were also interesting as they came either from an urban chicago background, or a white collar mafia background, both very unique and threatening... All the characters in this game are very forgettable. You have 5 characters on the 'good' side who are all interchangable in terms of skillset and annoying quipiness, and the villains are even more forgettable then that. One guy had a man-bun and that was the most interesting thing about ANY of them. If you appreciate story elements when playing an open world game, the First Watch Dogs game is far more interesting than the 2nd one. 

2)  The setting feels too kiddish... The first watch dogs takes place in Chicago where bad shit is going down. You have a serial killer running around leaving behind bodies, theres a sex trafficking auction ring you have to go deep in to dismantle, gangs all over the place, and cops who dont think twice before shooting. Its a solid and high octane environment to try to fight through in a video game. Watch Dogs 2 on the other hand takes place in San Francisco where a portion of the game code is set aside to taking selfies at certain landmarks around the city. The only R-rated mission takes place in a DLC (problems with that explained later) so it feels like you can just rampage through missions wearing bubble wrap with no feeling of consequence if something goes sideways. I've built cities in Cities Skylines that have more grime to them then San Francisco does in this game, and it kind of takes you out a little bit in terms of engagement

3)  The Physics engine is cartoonish... One of the most GLARING differences between Watch Dogs 1 and 2 that I immediately ran into is the physics animations. You kill someone in Watch Dogs 1, they fall over in a clump and stop moving. As expected. Youd think the same would be true for Watch Dogs 2 right? NOPE. Take down one enemy with a physical takedown and their body keeps moving for 10 seconds after theyre dead. And I dont mean 'arm twitching out' for a little bit. I mean entire bodies are bouncing around hallways like literal ping-pong balls. I cant prove it, but Im willing to bet somewhere in development they figured 'oh this would be funny and will get views' so they turned the physics reactions up to 500% to try to maximize the silliness of the game to try to generate buzz that way. Its not funny though, its outlandish and breaks your immersion even harder than the mediocrity of the rest of the game 

4) Some of the DLC regularly crashes your game... I purchased the both of them just to knock out some achievements in the Steam Library. I dont know which one it was, but one of them after completing any online mission has I shit you not a 80% crash rate for your game, forcing you to restart the mission once you get your computer to do a full reboot. THAT got annoying real quick, and was never an issue for me in the first Watch Dogs game

As for the positives

1)  More character customization and vehicle selection, which gives you something to actually spend money on. I end up with more money than I know what to do with in the first game, Watch Dogs 2 gives you enough material to make you have to consider budgeting 

2)  The Hacking Minigame added to the environment around you rather than just being on a cyber-screen-plane is a nice touch that adds a new element to breaking into things 

3)  The multiplayer actually works and you can play co=op with other players seamlessly unlike my experience with the First Watch Dogs 

4)  The game goes on sale fairly regularly so this can actually become a reaosnable buy and play if you wait for the right moment to purchase. Im parked right at around 50 hours which for a grand price of maybe $7 for the game and two DLC's is pretty solid when its all said and done. My opinion would have been far more negative if I spent closer to $50 on this with an extra $15 for the DLC's

5)  Hacking ability that can go through walls towards controllable equipment makes things a lot easier to plan and sort out compared to the 1st Watch Dogs game where your environment does frequently act as a barrier. Yes that trades immersion and reality for easiness and lower skill ceiling, but I dont mind it. 

Overall, not bad by itself, but compared to the 1st one it is a bit of a disappointment, yet if you get it on a solid sale then maybe it becomes more justifiable as a purchase. Sorry to meander.

An underrated gem of Ubisoft games,  Watch_Dogs 2 is a final proof of concept of what WD1 started, it is quite different from the first game, which is an understatement. Tonally, it is more "lighter", a happy-go-lucky hacktivist, "FUCK THE SYSTEM!" type story, which is far cry(haha) from the more "personal" revenge plot of the vigilante hacker, Aiden Pierce. I would say that WD2, fits more with the hacker type character,  against the backdrop of a foggy San Francisco, right in the middle of Silicon Valley, where the tech-corporations are in it for themselves and screwing over their consumer base, where privacy is meaningless, and Personal Data is their currency, it is quite poignant how relevant that is today. DedSec San Francisco's primary goal is to stick it into Blume, and expose CTOS 2.0 for the surveillance and control tool that it is, where Marcus Holloway(you) is at the center of. 

For a 10 year old game, San Francisco is still a beautifully crafted open world cityscape, iconic landmarks and all! It is the most "dynamic" city simulation I have ever experienced, okay to be more specific, the random NPCs with the randomized CTOS profiles give them a layer of depth and a bit more personality even though, in the grand scheme of things, it doesn't really "mean" anything, but it's a lot more than other NPCs from other open-world games. At times, there are Bethesda-like random encounters and NPC activities that bring a lot of life to the virtual San Francisco. The Police-crime system is a lot more improved from the first game(and I'd say a lot better than a certain open-world game), random people will report a crime they've witness. Punching people, flashing your gun in front of cops, crashing into them, basically anything that would normally be deemed illegal and is witness by law enforcement will get you a wanted level and initiate a chase(which makes sense). Speaking of chases, it is a lot more challenging, the cops will chase you the the ends of the earth, by land, by air, AND by sea, you'll have to use all the tools at your disposal to achieve a successful getaway, which is a lot more fun. A lot more dynamic with the street gangs too, you have Russian, Chinese, Black and Latino gangs, which reflects the melting-pot culture of modern-day America, and yes, you can remotely initiate a gang war, gangs v. gangs, cops v. gangs, or a nice wholesome three-way to just create chaos. Overall, I'd say that, you are in the world but it exists around you and not for you. It creates this grandiose feeling that the world is way bigger that it seems.

Yep, you can play it co-op, with a friend or a rando, and some random online co-op missions and activities . completely optional though, so take that what you will.

Since this is the a Ubisoft game, it carries the problems that Ubi-games tend to have, namely, random collectibles scattered around the world, although completely optional, but it's just there for runtime, it's not that it's hard or challenging, it's that there's just A LOT of them, it feel like a boring chore than an intuitive gameplay mechanic. As far as Ubi-games go, it's quite mild than the more modern entries, such as the AC games of Far Cry games, where the maps are large, like gigantic, but are filled with superficial-bullshit that it still feels empty. It's best described by the saying; "as wide as the ocean but a  deep as a puddle", I don't remember who said this, but ctto. I would feel though that WD2 is not that, or not as much, it's is  more compact and concise, that the world itself, is it own identity without feeling like an empty shell, which deserves praise. Combat though is still a hit or miss, pretty much the same as the first, but with new tools such as the drone, gives the combat and stealth system a lot more depth, even if it feels like a crutch, I guess the the combat is quite brutal in order to incentivize stealth and more "remote" hacks, which is an interesting change of pace. 

Overall, Watch_Dogs 2 is a welcome entry into the series, and deserves more love and praise, definitely get on a sale. a good 7.5/10 game, on of the Ubisoft games of all time, would recommend.

Watch Dogs 2 is a huge step up from the first game and one of the most fun open-world experiences I’ve played. It swaps the gloomy tone for a colorful, witty, rebellious spirit, and Marcus Holloway is a charming, likable hero. His DedSec crew, with Wrench, Sitara, Josh and Horatio, are full of personality and make every mission feel lively, funny and surprisingly heartfelt. The story takes sharp, clever jabs at tech giants, social media and surveillance culture while still staying entertaining. The San Francisco Bay Area is gorgeous, from the Golden Gate Bridge and Silicon Valley campuses to sunny streets and busy neighborhoods, and the world is packed with details to explore. The hacking is the real star, since you can approach each mission through stealth, chaos, drones or pure creativity, and the RC jumper and quadcopter add a lot of freedom to the gameplay. The soundtrack is excellent, the side missions are enjoyable, and the co-op adds even more fun. Overall, it’s a stylish, smart and endlessly entertaining game that deserves far more praise than it gets. 9/10, highly recommended

★★★★★ – One of the most enjoyable open-world games I've ever played.

Watch Dogs 2 is honestly such an underrated gem. I absolutely love the atmosphere of San Francisco, the freedom to explore, and the way the game lets you approach missions in your own style.

What makes this game special for me is the hacking. There's something incredibly satisfying about controlling the environment, messing with enemies, hacking cars, cameras, and security systems without even having to step into a fight. You can be creative with almost everything.

I also genuinely enjoyed the characters, especially the chemistry between the DedSec crew. They bring so much personality and humor to the story. Marcus is a great protagonist, and the whole DedSec vibe makes the experience even more memorable.

The soundtrack, colorful world, smooth gameplay, and countless things to discover make it easy to lose track of time while playing.

Sure, the story isn't perfect, but honestly, the gameplay and overall experience make up for it.

If you love open-world games, hacking, freedom, and just having fun doing ridiculous things in a massive city, give this game a shot.

Still an absolute banger. No regrets buying it. ❤️

I am a big fan of the first game and while the story does take a step back in terms of tension, and grit, the gameplay, world, and mission design are all a massive step up. I enjoyed the main cast of characters, this is very much a Fast and Furious Mr. Robot esque tale as compared to the John Wick revenge story of the first game, but it is a lot of fun and I thought it was all executed quite nicely.

If you appreciate San Francisco, or are a lifelong Giants fan like myself, then you will so enjoy the way Ubisoft replicated that iconic city here. This is a world you can get lost in, and with the parkour, sandbox levels, and awesome gameplay there is a lot to do and have fun while doing it. Maybe I am alone in this but I think Ubisoft is a highly underrated publisher, they put out phenomenal games, I am not defending their business practices, but over and over I find myself playing titles from them and having a blast.

Watch Dogs 2 is a phenomenal game, it does not outstay its welcome, it offers the players incredible variety in how they tackle objectives, areas to free roam, and incredible fluid gameplay to bring it all together in a wonderful medley of hacking, gunplay, and movement.

At first, I didn’t really understand why everyone was raving so much about Watch Dogs 2. But it seems DedSec just needed some time to hack through my firewall.

And you know what? They succeeded.

San Francisco has become a fantastic playground for hacker mayhem, and the ability to tackle missions in different ways adds a special charm to the game. Want to play stealthily? Go right ahead. Want to turn everything around you into digital chaos? The game won’t stop you. And sometimes the best plan is simply to rev up the car and watch everything go haywire.

The characters deserve special praise. The DedSec team is so eccentric that it’s simply fun to watch them. There’s plenty of humor, absurdity, and brilliant satire on modern society.

I won’t say the game is perfect, but it definitely has character. And the most interesting thing is that at first I didn’t feel much of a desire to keep playing, but in the end I got so hooked that I didn’t even notice how I’d finished the whole game.

It’s official: my brain has been successfully recruited by DedSec. Ctrl + Alt + San Francisco!

San Francisco is the best open world I've ever been in. Not the biggest, not the most detailed, but the one I actually want to be in. I've spent hours with no objective, just driving around the bay with the radio on, watching pedestrians do dumb stuff because I put a duck on their phone. That's the whole game to me. The city is a character and it's the best one.

The hacking is what makes it a different game instead of "GTA with a gimmick." You can do every mission three or four different ways and the game doesn't care which one you pick. I've done stealth missions by just hacking a traffic light and letting a bus run someone over. I've done them by stealing a jetpack and being an idiot. I've done them by putting a tazer on one cop and a drone on the other and just standing there watching. The game makes you feel smart for being creative and that's rarer than it should be.

Marcus is the first open world protagonist I've actually liked. He's not a brooding silence machine, he's a Bay Area kid who's funny and angry and the banter with your crew is genuinely good writing. I've replayed the intro more times than I want to admit. The tone of the whole game is "heist movie" and it commits to that. It's not trying to be a serious political statement like the first one. You finish it feeling like you just got away with something, not like you watched a lecture.

The missions are short. Ten, fifteen minutes. That's the trap. You sit down to do one and look up and it's three hours later and you did eight of them and you were laughing at the last one. I can't count how many nights that's happened.

It's not perfect. The side content gets repetitive past like 60 hours. The story's second act is a bit of a slog. The combat is fine but not great. None of that matters because the core loop of "drive around SF, hack stuff, be an idiot with your crew" is the best I've had in an open world and I don't think I'm going to get that again.

I think about this game when I'm in a real city. I see a traffic light and I want to hack it. I see a pedestrian and I want to put a duck on their phone. I'd play it again tomorrow. Same streets, same missions, same crew, same everything.

Alexios and Kassandra are charismatic, fun and relatable characters. They even remind me of Ezio — the best character in the AC universe.
The map offers a huge variety of things to do: side quests, collectibles, forts to capture, battles for territory, sailing your ship or simply getting lost and enjoying the view.
For some people, that's too much. For me? Well, I wanted more!
The DLCs are fun, but they're not as grounded as the base game. If that's not your cup of tea, just stick to the main game.

Assassin's Creed Odyssey is very fun and the main story is pretty good. This is a pretty decent RPG game, but a terrible Assassin's Creed game. The stealth is very basic and a little janky at times when combined with the parkour system in this, which is a huge step down from the classic Assassin's Creed games. The fun parts are in the combat both on land and sea. I like how the different weapon types feel unique from each other, the abilities you unlock actually are useful while not being op, and how the game can genuinely be difficult at times without keeping you stuck at one part of the game for two hours straight (Except that one hog boss fight, fuck that pig). The game isn't too grindy compared to other RPG games, all you have to do is do some side quests alongside the main story and you should be the appropriate level for most of the time. And once you do get to the higher levels, you really do start to feel much more powerful. The game itself also looks great and I love the customization (thank god for transmog). Although I must say, a lot of the acting in this game is horrendous. Some actors are actually pretty good like Alexios, but many of the side characters feel like you just started watching a Tubi movie. If you're looking for a good Assassin's Creed game, then this one isn't it and you should play something like Black Flag or the Ezio Collection. But if you're looking for a good RPG game or just really like this period of Ancient Greece (like me), then this game might be worth your time.

But the quests become repetitive, sometimes demanding considerable time for an underwhelming payoff. “Was that seriouslyy it?” sums up a few of them. Some characters also have conspicuously similar faces, I occasionally couldn’t tell who was who, lol.

My biggest criticism is how the sheer abundance of side quests overshadows the main narrative. After so many diversions, I’d forget what was happening in the central story. It deserved greater prominence, stronger continuity and more sustained emotional momentum. Ik Ik repetition is part of the AC formula, but story wise, I’d say Odyssey is decent, though nothing exceptional.

Personally, I found both DLCs better than the main storyline. Their compelling narratives and memorable moments left a deeper impression, making them the highlight of my experience. No cap!

Despite the repetition, Odyssey’s world, combat and atmosphere kept drawing me back. Imo, it’s the 3rd best AC I’ve played so far. 

7/10

[h3] 📢 Verdict: GRAB [/h3]
[b]TLDR:[/b] 
Assassin's Creed Odyssey throws you into a massive, richly realized fragment of ancient Greece, packed with flexible gameplay, fun side quests, and standout DLCs that tie the franchise together.

[list]
[*] 🔄 [b]The Loop:[/b] 
There is a healthy blend of ranged, close combat, stealth, and puzzle gameplay available. Go loud or quiet - they’re both fun. Hunting down the Cult of Kosmos through clues is addictive, and so is the naval combat aboard the Adrestia (it even has sea shanties, and a few of them are bangers). The Mercenary system is a nice touch, though it is hilarious how relentless they can be. I had sessions where I took out at least half a dozen of them in barely a couple of hours because they just kept spawning. Pro tip: do not pay off your bounty, so you level up faster and get higher-level loot. There are plenty of side quests, and quite a number of them are interesting and play out like a mini-series. There will also be several occasions where completing quests a certain way provides different outcomes, though for main quest lines, this is often limited to different narrative options rather than the outcomes themselves. Let me save you some time though: there is no achievement for completing every point of interest. I did not check this until after completing about a third of the regions, but thank goodness I did, because it gets repetitive without adding much value. Focus on the story.

[*] 🎨 [b]The Vibe:[/b] 
Greece during the Peloponnesian War is a breathtakingly exceptional setting for a game like this, and it was nice to see mythos and history tied in together. Graphics are great, and the audio is fine. Please Ubisoft, stop reusing "Ezio's Family" and start making something fresh with each new title. Voice acting sometimes does not match the animations, but it is serviceable. Most importantly, the writing needs to be improved in future titles, alongside other details that would enhance the overall immersion. For example, compare the cutscenes and writing from the older titles with the newer ones. I don’t take issue with the use of procedural cutscenes, far from it, but they could be better.  

[*] ⚙️ [b]The Friction:[/b] 
The HUD has too much going on, though that could just be my preference. Thankfully, there are a lot of HUD customization options, and turning almost all of them off made all the difference. Performance is very stable overall. The only exception was a couple of POIs in the last third of The Fate of Atlantis DLC that dropped my framerate, which appears to be a game engine issue rather than my rig, though it did not ruin my experience. I also recommend grabbing an auto-looter mod off Nexus before starting. It saves a lot of time and button mashing.

[*] 🌐 [b]The Ecosystem:[/b] 
Get both of the DLCs. I have noticed people saying that Origins has the better story and Odyssey has the better gameplay. If we are talking about the base game, I agree, but the DLCs bring Odyssey right up to the same rank. Also, play the questline “A Great Escape,” (it’ll show up in Kephallonia) after completing everything else, because it feels like the true ending of Odyssey and bridges the gap to the other titles, especially Origins.
[/list]

IMO the best AC game thus far, followed closely by Black Flag, even though this one came out a few years ago now. Played mostly on PS4 when it first came out so I actually have more like 200hrs in it. Obviously there are both good and bad things, most of the bad things though are simply the franchise selling cosmetics for WAY too much, even years after it came out, and also the fact that you need DLC's to actually finish the full story. If you don't you're kinda left on a cliffhanger and it is unfortunate to get to that and just be disappointed that you've gotta spend another $50 to be satisfied with the ending. Of course this is an AC game so the gameplay itself is largely rinse and repeat from all the other more recent games, but if you've played them before you're gonna be prepared for that. But I will say the combat is way better than it was in previous games, seems like they just finetuned the combat from Origins. Whenever I get a new AC game I know what im gonna get gameplay wise, but it's the stories that make me, and many others, always come back for more. As someone who enjoys learning about history, the series itself is really great in that aspect. They truly do make an effort to be as realistic as possible when it comes to various peoples/societies and its clear that they do their research in many areas. Obviously that does not include all the mythology stuff that they're getting more and more into lately. This game in particular feels more like the devs wanted to show how ancient Greeks genuinely believed the world around them worked, instead of just throwing in a bunch of mythology stuff for funsies. I might be biased though because Ancient Greece is one of my favorite areas of history to study so the premise is right up my alley anyways. Also I REALLY liked how you could choose who to play, it makes things more interesting for sure. Additionally, I loved the incorporation of Ithaca from Homer's The Iliad (aka The Odyssey), that classic is so fascinating in many ways so it was neat to be able to explore the island and uncover various artifacts directly relating to the story.

Basically, if you like history, ancient Greece and their mythology, or the AC franchise in general, give it a go. But do try to get the DLC's at a reduced price bc that part is BS to me.
